messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Unusual auth success/failure heartbeat from edge cluster eu-west-1. 4.2k requests/min from ~1.1k unique IPs to /v1/auth/token over last 2m. Suspected probe pattern. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/d/edge/auth-heartbeat?panelId=3 :rotating_light:
oncall-anna: Acknowledged. I'm taking P1. Paging security and infra. oncall switching to me for 30m.
security-jose: I’m on it. Can you dump request sample + headers to gist? Focus on User-Agent, x-forwarded-for patterns, and any malformed jwt attempts.
oncall-anna: Pushing samples to https://gist.github.com/rw/abc123 (redacted IPs). Saw repeated UA: "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; heartbeatbot/1.0)" and a cluster of tokens that 401 then 200 rapidly.
infra-sre-kim: Looks like traffic amplification hitting auth proxy rate limiter. Suggest immediate edge-level throttle + block on 5 CIDR prefixes driving 55% of traffic. Will also enable per-ip soft ban at WAF.
eng-lex: If it's abusing session tokens we should consider forced short rotation for svc-account read-only keys used by the mobile SDK. Any signs of token exfil?
support-fatima: No customer tickets yet. Telemetry shows spike in failed logins but no increased 5xx. A few customers in EU reported slow auth page loads.
security-jose: Good call. @infra-sre-kim please capture any logs with potential token material and move to secure bucket. If tokens found, we need emergency rotation and revoke in Auth DB.
infra-sre-kim: Running blocking action now:
```
# block top abusive IP ranges
aws wafv2 update-web-acl --name edge-auth --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-1 --cli-input-json file://block-cidrs.json
# enable rate-based rule
aws wafv2 create-rate-based-rule --name rb-auth-probe --rate-limit 1000 --scope REGIONAL --region eu-west-1
```
Blocked 4 CIDRs (x.x.16.0/20, x.x.48.0/22, x.x.200.0/21, x.x.88.0/23). Enabling additional logging to secure-s3://redwood-incidents/3932109876-logs

oncall-anna: Confirmed: CPU on auth-proxy fell back to normal within 45s of block. 401->200 patterns reduced by 92%.
security-jose: Pulling logs now. Running quick grep for "Authorization: Bearer" in recent streams. If we find full bearer tokens in logs, we must rotate affected keys and notify customers per PD-1 policy.
eng-lex: I scanned gcloud audit and found one service-account key creation event ~10m prior from a CI job on staging; not production. Not seeing suspicious iam:generateAccessToken.
security-jose: Ok. Minimal scope so far. Still validate if tokens were exfiltrated via debug logs. @infra-sre-kim can you confirm if any S3 objects with auth headers were uploaded in the last 24h?
infra-sre-kim: Searching... found one debug log upload by svc-ci-batch at 2026-03-17T10:12Z to staging-logs.s3 that contains truncated auth headers. It was from a staging job and marked PII-redacted, but we will treat as potential exposure.
support-fatima: Customer impact: staging-only customers may be affected; production customers show latency blips only. No escalations from paying customers yet.
security-jose: Triage summary: active probe causing auth heartbeat surge; edge-level blocks mitigated immediate load. One staging debug upload contains truncated auth headers — low confidence of live token exfil. Actions: 1) Rotate staging service-account keys and revoke any tokens issued in last 2h. 2) Audit production logs for any unredacted tokens. 3) Post incident update to #status with mitigation summary. 4) Legal on standby.
legal-tom: Please add me to thread if customer notification becomes necessary. Keep timeline + artifacts.
oncall-anna: Doing rotations now for staging keys. Command:
```
# rotate staging svc key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new-key.json --iam-account=svc-staging@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# update CI to use new key
kubectl -n staging set secret generic svc-staging-key --from-file=new-key.json
# revoke old keys
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete old-key-id --iam-account=svc-staging@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Rotation complete. CI picked up new key; no failing jobs observed.
security-jose: I ran token-scan across last 6 hours in prod logs; no full bearer tokens found. Marking exposure risk as low.
eng-lex: Recommend we add an automated sanitizer that strips Authorization headers before debug log upload for all environments and add a CI gate to prevent key material in artifacts. Will open PR.
oncall-anna: Opening follow-up runbook ticket and scheduling 1h blameless postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Link: https://go/redwood/incidents/3932109876/postmortem
security-jose: Closing P1 to P2 for monitoring. Keeping thread open for 24h. Thanks everyone :heart:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: edge-auth probe mitigated at 3932109956. Final status: mitigated, low customer impact, rotation completed for staging keys.
